title: Admin Bridgelet: flow visualizer + idempotency checker for runbook tasks
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build an interactive 'bridgelet' for operator-runbooks that renders a directed execution graph, enables dry-run rehydration of a run (trace replay without side-effects), and runs an idempotency verifier across each step. The tool should surface non-idempotent operations, required permissions, and provide quick-replay snippets operators can paste into the admin REPL. This aims to reduce mean-time-to-repair by making runbook behavior transparent and preventing accidental destructive replays.
acceptance_criteria: Graph view shows nodes, canonical inputs, and average execution latency per step for the last 30 days
Dry-run rehydration can re-execute control flow with side-effects disabled and produce a divergence report
Idempotency checker flags steps that mutate external state without compensating actions and classifies severity
Operator quick-replay snippets are generated for each node in bash and admin-repl formats
Security gating honors RBAC: only users in admin role can run side-effecting replays
Integration tests covering simulated run replay and idempotency detection exist and pass in CI
implementation_notes: Backend: extend runbook metadata API to emit execution traces (step id, input hash, output hash, start/end timestamps)
Idempotency fingerprint: compute stable fingerprint from step type + parameter schema + observed side-effect hashes
UI: new visualization canvas in Admin Console (canvas component reused from Console-telemetry), with pan/zoom and step-detail flyout
Safety: dry-run layer implemented as a request interceptor that toggles downstream calls to stubbed clients via feature-flag
Telemetry: wire events to ops.telemetry: run_replay_started, run_replay_divergence, idempotency_flagged
Fallback: when traces unavailable, show estimated graph from runbook static template and mark as 'partial'
Security: require security review before enabling side-effecting replay (security_review_required=true)
